newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine pilots say six near collisions in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Argentine pilots say six near collisions in 1997.

text.p: Shaky air traffic control systems have caused six near mid-air collisions over Argentina already this year, the Argentine Airline Pilots Association said on Wednesday.
In the most recent case, a DC9 jet operated by Argentine airline Austral had to stop increasing altitude to avoid a United Airlines Boeing 767 heading for Buenos Aires' Ezeiza airport on April 10.
"If the pilot had continued to fly higher, he would have hit the back of the American plane," pilot's association spokesman Gonzalo Ruiz Suhr told Reuters.
The pilots believe Argentina's air force -- which controls all air traffic in the country -- must install more equipment such as radar and improve training for pilots and air traffic controllers.
An air force spokesman told Reuters the incidents were under investigation but it appeared that at least some of the near disasters reported by the pilots were exaggerated.
"We think they have been too quick to judge what has happened. There have been cases where air traffic control has been deficient, but this has not been demonstrated in every case," he said.
Pilots and air force officials began a series of meetings on Tuesday to discuss ways to improve air safety.

Argentina's airports were due to be privatised this year, but the sale has been preceded by a series of embarrassing incidents. In one of the more disturbing cases, someone beamed powerful radio waves at Ezeiza in an apparent attempt to interfere with radar.
